headline: HC orders 43rd BCS non-cadre results to be re-published within 60 days
summary: The High Court called the recruitment process 'opaque' and ordered the Public Service Commission to finalize appointments based on merit.
details: The High Court has ordered the republication of results for non-cadre positions in the 43rd BCS, with the recruitment process to be completed within 60 days.
A bench comprising Justice Shashanka Shekhar Sarkar and Justice Urmi Rahman delivered the verdict on Thursday.
The ruling follows a writ petition filed by 465 candidates, including Maruf Hossain, who challenged the validity of the recommendation of 642 people for non-cadre posts in January 2024.
The court expressed surprise and termed the recruitment process as 'opaque' and not in accordance with the law.
Lawyer Mohammad Humayun Kabir, representing the petitioners, stated that the PSC had recommended 642 candidates without publishing the final results, which led to the legal challenge.
The court had previously ordered the preservation of 8,501 non-cadre posts in the 43rd BCS during preliminary hearings.
According to the petitioners' lawyer, there are a 12,551 non-cadre posts available for candidates of the 43rd BCS based on government demand.

headline: Mother, two daughters killed in Lakshmipur attack
summary: A mother and two daughters were hacked to death in Raipur, while a third daughter was critically injured. A suspect was beaten by a mob, and several police officers were injured by brickbats.
details: A mother and two of her daughters were hacked to death in a rented house in the Godown Road area of Raipur Municipality, Lakshmipur, on Thursday morning.
The deceased have been identified as Shahinur Begum (38), her elder daughter Saima Akhter (21), a Dhaka University student, and her younger daughter Shifa Akhter (9).
The middle daughter, 17-year-old Ikra Akhter, a student at Raipur Kazi Faruki College, was sent to a hospital in Dhaka in critical condition.
An unidentified youth, suspected of being involved in the incident, was caught and beaten by an agitated crowd before being sent to Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital for treatment.
Six to seven police personnel were injured by brickbats thrown by the crowd as they tried to bring the situation under control.
The victims hailed from Cumilla district but had been renting a place in Lakshmipur for many years. Shahinur's husband had died of electrocution a few years ago.
According to the Raipur Upazila Health and Family Planning Officer, all victims had injuries from sharp weapons on various parts of their bodies.
Police have brought the situation under control and the bodies of the deceased are currently at the hospital.
